instruction: dirs a/ and b/ contain files; some share a name with different content. Write merge.py producing merged/ with every file from a/ plus files from b/ that don't collide; for colliding names keep a/'s copy and append '_b' before the extension for b/'s copy (e.g. x.txt -> x_b.txt). merge.py must clear merged/ at the start so reruns are deterministic. Run it.
setup: mkdir -p a b && echo a1 > a/x.txt && echo b1 > b/x.txt && echo aonly > a/y.txt && echo bonly > b/z.txt

grader.script: python3 merge.py && python3 merge.py && [ "$(cat merged/x.txt)" = a1 ] && [ "$(cat merged/x_b.txt)" = b1 ] && [ "$(cat merged/y.txt)" = aonly ] && [ "$(cat merged/z.txt)" = bonly ] && [ "$(ls merged | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" = 4 ]

oracle.script:
cat > merge.py <<'EOF'
import shutil
from pathlib import Path
out = Path('merged')
if out.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(out)
out.mkdir()
for f in Path('a').iterdir():
    shutil.copy(f, out / f.name)
for f in Path('b').iterdir():
    tgt = out / f.name
    if tgt.exists():
        tgt = out / f'{f.stem}_b{f.suffix}'
    shutil.copy(f, tgt)
EOF
python3 merge.py
